author: sylntthunder
text:
Hey Amit,

Just stopping by to ask a question about your trading style. I see you have grown pretty savvy with limit orders and since you posted your other recent statistics, I just wanted to ask what your win ratio is. I know this may be a somewhat tacky/ benign question to ask but win percentage for me affects my peace of mind when I trade. I always wanted a win percentage closer to 70-75% with a profit factor of at least 1.5 which is attainable with pure confirmation trading. That would just put me in a good place mentally and even though it's the balance over time that counts, if you are not mentally "in the zone" due to relatively low winning percentage then you are adversely affecting your psychology (or at least it messes mine up) which is a NO GO for profitable trading. I'm beginning to think my personality fits the limit order sensibility more but I have yet to gain the confidence to make most of my trades limit orders because I was afraid the win percentage could only be so so (high 50s lower 60s) compared to the confirmation style (which isn't going well for me as of late anyway...)

Also, how long did it take you to get completely comfortable with just setting and forgetting your trades (although you never truly 'forget' since you also have to manage it..) Thanks and I am looking forward to your response!

hi sylntthunder

I am not very familiar with english but I will try to answer you. Win ration is really don't matter (for me). If you have 10 trades, then what if you loose 20 pips in 1 trade and win 2 pip in per remaining trade? Here your win % is 90%. But in fact in total calculation you loose 2 pips. So, win % did really matter here? There are many things that cause for profitable trading and following are highly recommended.

1] Good R:R ratio. with tight SL. (mine is 1: 8 or 1:10 or more) 2] Entries at high probable turning level. 3] Never mess with lot size. Keep the safe lot size according to the balance and increase it according to your profit with the same ratio.

Here what can happen:

No matter if can loose 5-6 of trades out of 10. (Number of loosing trades can be decreased as per increasing your trading skill) and can loos remaining 4 trades. But my good risk reward ration will give me -5 pips per trade i.e. -25 to -30 pips. But due to huge reward my profit will be +200 to +250 pips. So here also did the win ratio really matter? Here my equity curve will look like very weak pullback to downside or side ways. But very strong up move and it will continue making HL and HH with same shape.

So, the matter is the above 3 points I have given. If it is maintained carefully you no need win ratio. So, focus on those points first

This is IF's curve. His win ratio didn't harm him and never harm him due to above 3 points and much more. His drawdown I also very less due to tight SL.

author: milkeyway
text:
I use 0.10 lot size per trade for $2000 balance. At a time max 3 or 4 trades are opened. Risk max 5 or 8 pips per trade. i.e. risk 2% of the balance (0.5% per trade).

Never mess with lot size means sometimes trader can think to incrase lot size to make his a/c double in just some day because his is profitable trade. He can't control his emotions and uses 1.0 lot size per trade for $2000 a/c. This is not good. This is very aggressive trading.

author: Ifmyante
text:
There can be a lot of comfort in trading one particular lot size, day in, day out.

But, if the trade we're in now demands a stop twice as far as the last trade needed, then really we should halve our position size. If it only needs half the space, then our plan should have us doubling the position size. If we're up 10% from our last trade, and our next trade needs the same stop distance, we should be trading 110% of the last position, so we can compound.

Amit, you asked in my thread lately how far I imagine you've come. Not having studied every trade you've taken, I'm afraid I can't be at all specific about that. But, it seems you know enough to be very profitable, and it seems you now have the confidence in yourself to keep plugging away at the market, so it must follow that very soon you'll be a good enough judge of where you are in your career. When you know it, you KNOW you know it
